prompt: Problem 1 (Urban forest tree-species mapping). Predict the relative basal area (RBA) of tree species from remote-sensing data (AVIRIS hyperspectral reflectance — ~182 bands and derived canopy chemistry/indices — and lidar-derived structure metrics) measured on field plots. Predicted RBAs across species must sum to ≤ 1.
parts: A. Conduct EDA assessing the relation between RBA and lidar/hyperspectral data, using a specific dimension-reduction method and visualizations.

B. Using hyperspectral data, build predictive models for the proportion of (1) white oak, (2) white pine, (3) ash, with statistical evaluation of prediction performance and variable importance; ensure the three predicted RBAs sum to ≤ 1 on any future data.
C. Repeat B using the lidar data.
D. Explore combining both remote-sensing data types for each of the three species, and argue for or against combining them.
E. Recommend the essential next steps for mapping tree-species composition from remote sensing, with reasoning.
notes: Prof. Sijian Wang. Dataset committed in repo (Applied Exam 2019 packet). Transcribed from extracted text.
data: Downloads/past-PhD exams/Applied Exam 2019 packet/Tree Species Data and Descriptions.xlsx

prompt: Problem 2 (Gaussian-process regression). Generate 7 equally spaced points $x_1, \dots, x_7$ on $[0,1]$ and responses $Y(x) = e^{-1.4x}\cos(\frac{7\pi x}{2})$.
parts: (1) For the GP model $Y(x) = \mu + Z(x)$ with $\operatorname{cov}[Z(x+h), Z(x)] = \sigma^2\phi(h;\theta)$, $\phi(h;\theta) = \exp(-\theta h^2)$, write the MLE expressions for $\mu, \theta, \sigma^2$ and compute them from the 7 observations.
(2) Write the BLUP of $Y(x_0)$ and its (plug-in) predictive distribution.
(3) Generate 1000 equally spaced points $x_j^*$ on $(0,1)$ and the corresponding true responses.
(4) Compare MLE-EBLUP predictions at the $x_j^*$ with the true values via a plot.
(5) Add 95% predictive confidence bands to the plot from (4).
(6) Prove the BLUP is an interpolator and demonstrate it using (4)-(5).
(7) Fit a spline-based interpolating model on the same 7 points; compare GP vs spline prediction performance on the test data and comment on any non-performance advantages/disadvantages.
notes: Prof. Ying Hung. Self-contained simulation. Transcribed from extracted text.
